==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{l|en|appretiate}} {{qualifier|archaic}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per-|id=before}}
Originated 1645–55; from {{bor|en|la-med|appreciātus||valued or appraised}}, later variant of {{der|en|la-lat|appretiātus||appraised}}, the {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|appretiō}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix|nocat=1}}), from {{af|la|ad-|pretium|-ō|alt1=a(d)|t1=toward|alt2=preti(um)|t2=price|id3=denominal|pos3=first conjugation verb-forming suffix|nocat=1}}.

Cognate to {{cog|fr|apprécier}}. Latin root also origin of English {{doublet|notext=1|en|appraise}}, which has various Romance cognates; see also {{m|en|precious}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{a|en|RP|GA|Canada}} {{IPA|en|/əˈpɹiː.ʃi.eɪt/|/əˈpɹiː.si.eɪt/|/əˈpɹɪʃ.i.eɪt/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-appreciate.ogg|Audio (US)}}
* {{a|en|General Australian}} {{IPA|en|/ˈəˈpɹiː.ʃi.æɪt/}}
* {{hyphenation|en|ap|pre|ci|ate}}
* The pronunciation with {{IPAchar|/ʃ/}} is the result of [[regressive assimilation]], where the transition between the unstressed {{IPAchar|/i/}} and the following vowel generates a phonetic palatal glide {{IPAchar|[j]}} that pulls the tongue back toward the hard palate during the production of the alveolar sibilant. While this sequence fully collapses in words with weak suffixes (such as {{m|en|social}}), the unstressed {{IPAchar|/i/}} and its subsequent glide are retained here to preserve metrical rhythm before the secondarily stressed suffix {{m|en|-ate}}. The pronunciation with {{IPAchar|/s/}} preserves the unassimilated sibilant. See [[w:Phonological history of English consonant clusters#Regressive assimilation and suffix stress]].

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To be [[grateful]] or [[thankful]] for.
#: {{syn|en|esteem|acknowledge}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''appreciate''' your efforts.}}
#: {{ux|en|We sincerely '''appreciate''' your help.}}
#: {{ux|en|Any aid will be warmly '''appreciated'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|I'd '''appreciate''' it so much if you'd keep me abreast of developments.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To view as [[valuable]].
#: {{syn|en|cherish|esteem|value|Thesaurus:hold dear}}
#: {{ux|en|You must learn to '''appreciate''' time.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To be fully [[conscious]] of; [[understand]]; be [[aware]] of; [[detect]].
#: {{nearsyn|en|realize<id:become aware of, understand, or appreciate>|grasp|acknowledge}}
#: {{ux|en|It is essential for the reader to '''appreciate''' how important this argument is.}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''appreciate''' that what I'm asking you to do is very difficult.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1949|author={{w|Friedrich Hayek|F. A. Hayek}}|title=The Intellectuals and Socialism|journal={{w|University of Chicago Law Review}}|publisher={{w|University of Chicago}}|location={{w|Chicago}}|volume=16|number=3|doi=10.2307/1597903|page=419|passage=It is rather the person whose general knowledge is supposed to qualify him to '''appreciate''' expert testimony, and to judge between the experts from different fields, whose power is enhance.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|transitive}} To increase in value.
#: {{syn|en|bedear|endear}}
#: {{ant|en|depreciate}}
#: {{ux|en|The value of his portfolio '''appreciated''' by 80% over eight years.}}
#* {{RQ:Landon Romance|page=234|volume=I|passage=Laughter may be generally classed under three heads,—forced, silly, or vulgar; but hers is the most sweet, real, ''spirituelle'' sound possible—it so '''appreciates''' the wit, which it increases as it catches—it speaks of spirits so fresh, so youthful!}}

====Usage notes====
* This is a [[catenative]] verb that takes the ''gerund (-ing)''. See [[Appendix:English catenative verbs]]

====Alternative forms====
* {{l|en|appretiate}} {{qualifier|archaic}}
* {{l|en|'preciate}} {{q|pronunciation spelling}}

====Derived terms====
{{col|en|appreciatable|appreciater|appreciator|apprecihate|disappreciate|misappreciate|reappreciate|underappreciate|much appreciated}}

====Related terms====
* {{l|en|appraise}}
* {{l|en|appreciation}}
* {{l|en|appreciative}}
* {{l|en|precious}}
